hello.note: Oy! or Uy! is how friends hail each other on the street.

goodbye.note: Amping! (take care) is the warmer, more Bisaya farewell.

how_are_you.note: Cebuano has no po/opo; respect shifts the pronoun instead, e.g. Kumusta mo? to elders or strangers.

thank_you.note: Daghang salamat (thanks a lot) adds warmth without any particle.

youre_welcome.note: Rivals Ok ra to oy and Wala ra to oy (very casual, peers only); Walay sapayan is the neutral everyday reply.

no_problem.note: Contraction of Walay problema; an offhand, casual reply to thanks, calqued on English no problem.

please.note: Stands alone before the request, unlike Tagalog's paki- prefix: Palihog ihatag (please give). Palihug is a common informal spelling.

excuse_me.note: Said when passing by or interrupting; pair with Palihog to get someone's attention first.

sorry.note: Literally forgive me; casually Pasensya na (bear with me) is also heard.

no.note: Dili negates a statement or verb; Wala (there isn't/none) answers existence questions.

of_course.note: Gyud is the Bisaya emphasis particle (like Tagalog talaga); Syempre! is the common Tagalog-borrowed alternative.

amazing.note: Kaayo is the Bisaya intensifier, equivalent to Tagalog napaka-.

delicious.note: Lami is the iconic Bisaya word for tasty; Namit is a common Mindanao Cebuano variant.

cheers.note: Names the Visayan custom of passing one shared glass around the tagayan circle.
